newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds open stronger, outperform U.S. issues.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds open stronger, outperform U.S. issues.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened stronger on Wednesday, with long bonds outperforming U.S. Treasuries, helped by a stronger dollar and waning concerns about supply.

"We have lagged behind the U.S. for the past few sessions as the U.S. has gone like gangbusters. Fundamentally what we may be getting here is a little bit of catch-up, a catch-up warranted by getting over the hurdle of supply pressure, plus the currency stabilizing," said Michael Gregory, a fixed-income economist and strategist with Lehman Brothers.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.64 to C$121.87 to yield 6.355 percent.
Like yesterday, the Canadian 30-year set a record by trading with the lowest yield in its history.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 15/32 to yield 6.35 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowed to one basis point from two basis points at Tuesday's close.
Gregory said the impetus for the rise in Canada does come from the United States, where the bond market extended overnight gains as investors remain convinced inflation is no immediate threat.
Gains in the currency helped Canadian bonds to build on those gains and outperform the U.S. market.
Canada's dollar opened firmer on Wednesday at C$1.3835 (US$0.7228), helped by an Australian rate cut, then rallied towards C$1.38 (US$0.7246).
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.27 to C$110.39 to yield 5.843 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 7/32 to yield 6.08 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 24 basis points from 23 basis points at Tuesday's close.
